Judgment:

1. By this order, I shall dispose of the petitioner filed by the claimants for the unfortunate death of the deceased Rohit Kapasia in a road traffic accident occurred on 31.10.2020 at abut 7.00 am at IMT Ring Road.
The deceased has left behind his wife, two sons and parents as his legal heirs.

2. The facts of this case need not to be having any big canvas:-
"On 31.10.2020, the husband of the petitioner was going to supply the milk to sector 2 Faridabad on his motorcycle, suddenly a bullet motorcycle bearing no. HR- 29-AL-1377 being driven in a rash and negligent manner had hit the deceased.
Resulting to which, deceased fell down and sustained fatal injuries.
He was taken to the B.K. Hospital, Faridabad, Haryana where he was died."

sentences.text: Counsel for the insurance company has rebutted the arguments stating that as per verification report of the driving license of the investigator, the driver of the offending vehicle was driving a motorcycle with gears on a driving license for motorcycle without gears on the day of the accident.
The driver did not possess a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident which is why he had been challaned under Section 3/181 of the Motor Vehicle Act in the charge sheet.

Hence, the owner having permitted to the driver to drive the vehicle knowing fully well that the driver did not possess a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and has committed breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy.

sentences.text: Insurance company had examined the witness R3W1 to buttress her contention that respondent no. 1 was driving the motorcycle without having any license, so he was challaned.
He did not have any license to drive the motorcycle with gear.
He has possessed only the driving the two wheeler without gear.
So she submits that owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and condition of the insurance policy, so the recovery rights be given to him.

31.Entire case of the respondent no. 3 is that there is a violation in terms of the insurance policy of the motorcycle because the respondent no. 1 does not possess the driving license of the class of vehicle.
However, there is no difference in skill to drive a motorcycle/ two wheeler with gear or without gear.
Even, in the four wheeler, licensing department issuing the driving licesne does not distinguish whether the four wheeler car is having with gear of without gear.
Skill to drive the two wheeler is the same.
A person has to balance the two wheeler by his skill not by the way that it was for without gear of with gear.
Therefore, the plea of the respondent no. 1 is not sustainable.
Liability falls upon the respondent no. 3 which is contractually liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
He submitted that the maximum compensation be granted to the petitioners.
The driver did not possess a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident which is why he had been challaned under Section 3/181 of the Motor Vehicle Act in the charge sheet.
Hence, the owner having permitted to the driver to drive the vehicle knowing fully well that the driver did not possess a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and has committed breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy.
Hence, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
is well settled law that where petition under Section 166 of the Act is instituted, it becomes the duty of the petitioner to establish rash and negligent driving by the driver.
In a petition under Motor Vehicles Act, Tribunal need not go into the technicality because strict rules of procedure and evidence are not followed.
Basically, in Mrs. Aadesh and ors Vs Saumay Sharma and ors. 17.01.2023 Page No. 10 of 25 road accident cases, Tribunal has simply to quantify the compensation which is just rational and reasonable on the basis of enquiry.
Though it is an admitted legal position that the negligence on the part of driver with respect to the use of vehicle needs to be established but the same is to be established on the principles of preponderance of probabilities as decided in New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Harsh Mishra & Ors. III(2015) ACC 435 Delhi.
16.
No doubt, herein the charge sheet has been filed against the respondent no. 1 making him negligent of his act of driving of his motorcycle.
Consequent thereto, claimant's husband was died.
Petitioner had tried to prove his case while leading the evidence of PW 2 who was behind the motorcycle of the deceased and had been coming in the car.
It is also the matter of fact that it is the head on collision between the two motorcycle.
Both the motorcycles were damaged badly.
Even, the respondent no. 1 had sustained injury and admitted in the hospital.
Considering the above facts that the charge sheet has been filed against the respondent no. 1, yet petitioner/ deceased had also contributed his part / negligence in occurrence of the accident.
He was taking two canes of milk in the motorcycle essentially cover more space than the motorcycle should have.
However, nothing has been brought on record whether there is enough space or no space in passing two motorcycles in the congested traffic.
Therefore, at least, the compensation which is to be Mrs. Aadesh and ors Vs Saumay Sharma and ors. 17.01.2023 Page No. 11 of 25 awarded be deducted at least 15% from the head of future loss of income.
17.Now, the court has to assess as to how much compensation be awarded to the petitioners and by whom.
Deceased was died at the spot.
Therefore, all the five petitioners being the wife, two minor sons, mother and father of the deceased are entitled to consortium.
As far as the head of Loss of Dependency is concerned, same is to be calculated as per the multiplier method which has been adopted as a thumb rule in Sarla Verma vs.
DTC [2009 (6) Scale 129] and various other judgments, unless there are exceptional circumstances which make it necessary to depart from the said rule.
Further, in the judgment titled as National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (Supra) it has been concluded by the Hon'ble Supreme Court that in determination of the multiplicand the deduction for personal and living expenses the Tribunals shall be guided by the law as laid in Sarla Verma's case.
Except the fact, that the deceased was carrying two motorcycle, does not mean that he was carrying the business of dairy.
However,
considering the fact that deceased was resident of Haryana, therefore, minimum wages of Haryana of unskilled worker for assessing the future loss.
He did not have any license to drive the motorcycle with gear.
He has possessed only the driving the two wheeler without gear.
So she submits that owner of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and condition of the insurance policy, so the recovery rights be given to him.
31.Entire case of the respondent no. 3 is that there is a violation in terms of the insurance policy of the motorcycle because the respondent no. 1 does not possess the driving license of the class of vehicle.
However, there is no difference in skill to drive a motorcycle/ two wheeler with gear or without gear.
Skill to drive the two wheeler is the same.
A person has to balance the two wheeler by his skill not by the way that it was for without gear of with gear.
Liability falls upon the respondent no. 3 which is contractually liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
opennyai_summary.decision:
After adding future prospects, the income of the deceased comes to Rs. 13,241/- (Rs. 9,458/- + 9,458/- x 40/ 100).
Legal heirs i.e., petitioner no.1 to 5 can be said to be dependent upon the income of the deceased being the wife, two minor sons, mother and father of the deceased.
Therefore, one-fourth is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses.
After deduction, the income of the deceased comes to 9,931/-.
Thus, the loss of dependency comes to Rs. 21,45,096/- (Rs. 9,931/- x 12 x 18).
I therefore, award Rs.
21,45,096/- to the petitioners towards loss of dependency.
After deducting the 15% of contributory negligence from this amount, it comes to Rs. 18,23,332/-.
